classification.difficultyReason: Same structure as p80-q1: a logistic solve with unknown C, two data points and algebra to isolate C. The numbers simplify the exponential slightly.

content.prompt:
The barramundi population $P$ in a dam satisfies

$$\frac{dP}{dt}=0.25P\left(1-\frac{P}{C}\right),$$

where $t$ is years after stocking and $C$ is the carrying capacity.

At stocking there were $12\,000$ barramundi; 4 years later there were $24\,000$.

Use $\dfrac{C}{P(C-P)}=\dfrac{1}{P}+\dfrac{1}{C-P}$ to find the carrying capacity, to the nearest thousand.

answer.worked:
Separate variables and use the supplied partial fractions:
$$\begin{aligned}
\int\left(\frac1P+\frac1{C-P}\right)\,dP&=\int0.25\,dt\\
\ln|P|-\ln|C-P|&=0.25t+k\\
\frac{P}{C-P}&=Ae^{0.25t}.
\end{aligned}$$
At $t=0$, $P=12\,000$; at $t=4$, $P=24\,000$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{12\,000}{C-12\,000}&=A\\
\frac{24\,000}{C-24\,000}&=Ae.
\end{aligned}$$
Divide the second equation by the first:
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{2(C-12\,000)}{C-24\,000}&=e\\
2(C-12\,000)&=e(C-24\,000)\\
(e-2)C&=24\,000(e-1)\\
C&=\frac{24\,000(e-1)}{e-2}\\
C&\approx57\,000.
\end{aligned}$$
The carrying capacity is $57\,000$ barramundi, to the nearest thousand.
